steps.name: next_invoice_estimate -- Pro-plan overage projection
criteria: Overage per dimension = max(0, usage - pro_included) / overageUnit x PRICING.overage[dimension] (e.g. 620,000 overage reads => $0.31)
Storage overage uses a flat per-GB rate, not the per-100k unit the other three dimensions use
Total = base + sum of all overage line items
Zero overage across all dimensions shows base-only messaging, not a zero-itemized breakdown
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the RED panic in data::next_invoice_estimate(usage: UsageTotals, plan: Plan) -> NextInvoiceEstimate. Reads/writes/deletes overage = max(0, usage[dim] - PRICING.pro_included[dim]) / PRICING.overage_unit * PRICING.overage_rate[dim] (matches the story's worked example: 620,000/100,000 x $0.05 = $0.31 for reads). Storage overage = usage.storage_gb * PRICING.storage_per_gb -- a flat per-GB rate, deliberately NOT divided by the 100k unit the other three dimensions use; this distinction is exactly what storage_overage_uses_flat_gb_rate_not_per_100k_unit guards against regressing. total = PRICING.base + sum(all overage line items); when every dimension's overage is 0, the caller renders '$49.00 base - no overage projected' instead of a zero-itemized breakdown. NextInvoiceCard (overview.rs, Pro-plan only per AC-103-01/AC-102-04) also carries the fixed 'Estimated - projecting to period end' label and the illustrative-pricing footer disclosure (AC-103-05/06) -- both are static markup, not exercised by these TEA-state tests but required production work for this step. [FIX 2026-08-11 by orchestrator: verified exact signature from the test file -- data::next_invoice_estimate(usage: &UsageTotals) -> NextInvoiceEstimate, NO plan parameter (tests call it with just &usage). Estimate struct needs fields: has_overage: bool, total, base, overage_reads, overage_writes, overage_deletes, overage_storage (all f64). PRICING needs: pro_included: UsageTotals, pro_base, overage_rate_per_gb_storage, plus per-dimension overage rates -- check exact field names PRICING already has vs needs adding. All 4 tests are data.rs-layer only, no view assertion -- overview.rs likely does NOT need touching per established discipline, verify against test file.]

free_cap_exceeded is only ever reachable when the account is actually on the Free plan (property)
A Pro-plan account is never shown as free_cap_exceeded (property)
read_only() is true if and only if effective_status() != Active (property)

This single symbol is what both the banner-presence tests AND the two clicking_*_cta tests exercise -- the CTA tests assert on the returned cta_msg value, not a live DOM click, since OpenCardModal/OpenUpgradeModal themselves were already implemented in 01-01. Both methods stay pure reads over existing fields, per the DDD-8/AC-108-06 constraint -- do not add a cached bool anywhere on AppModel. [FIX 2026-08-11 by orchestrator: steps 07-01 and 07-02 MERGED. Original 07-01 (suspension_banner_view) architecturally calls effective_status()/read_only() internally per this feature's single-sourced status-derivation constraint (wave-decisions.md) -- splitting them with 07-01 scheduled before 07-02 made 07-01 impossible to reach GREEN (suspension_banner_view would call a still- panicking effective_status()). Implement effective_status()/read_only() FIRST within this merged step, then suspension_banner_view() on top of them, in that internal order, within a single TDD RED/GREEN/COMMIT cycle.] [FIX 2026-08-11 by orchestrator, second pass: AppModel::effective_status() was ALREADY implemented ahead of schedule as a side effect of step 04-02 (its test genuinely required it) -- committed 2ce84dd. Do NOT reimplement it, only read_only() and suspension_banner_view() remain as real scaffolds.
